record.paper: Pure pairs. II. Excluding all subdivisions of a graph

dossier_meta.paper: Pure pairs. II. Excluding all subdivisions of a graph
dossier_meta.statement_text: Let $H$ be a graph and let $P$ be a forest of $H$. Then every coherent ideal contains a $P$-filleting of $H$.
dossier_meta.context_text: The paper's main theorem (2.3) proves the statement when $P$ is a path of $H$. The authors propose this strengthening, noting it would be best possible since the conclusion fails when $P$ contains a cycle of $H$ (as coherent ideals can have arbitrarily large girth). If true, it would imply the main theorem of [8] (strong Erdős-Hajnal property for all forests) in the same way Theorem 2.3 implies the main theorem of [18].
